result.title: ABSClaw: From Invented Worlds to Reality-Grounded Social Simulation
result.summary: LLM-based artificial societies exhibit rich behavior but often lack scientific grounding: personas and environments are assumed, interaction networks are synthetic, and simulators are generated as free-form code, making results difficult to tie to real populations and sensitive to the backbone model. We argue that simulated worlds should be sampled from observed data, while simulation logic should be implemented by composing operations from a shared, task-independent vocabulary. In this paper, we introduce ABSClaw, a zero-code agent that compiles natural-language requests into executable, reality-grounded social simulations. ABSClaw grounds who acts, where they act, and with whom they interact in survey and census data, geospatial sources, and real networks. It expresses state transitions through 26 atomic operations. To support an open and extensible ecosystem, ABSClaw further allows capabilities to be added as lifecycle-scoped skills without modifying its core. Furthermore, we propose ABSBench, a benchmark of 193 real-world social-simulation tasks. On ABSBench, ABSClaw achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated social simulators. Three real-world case studies show that grounding personas, environments, and interaction networks each improves agreement with observed outcomes. With one runtime skill, ABSClaw executes 13 population-scale simulations, collectively involving 25 million agents. Together, these results demonstrate ABSClaw's real-world fidelity, extensibility, and scalability.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ABSClaw：一个将自然语言请求编译为基于调查、人口普查、地理与真实网络数据的多智能体社会模拟系统，并用 26 个原子操作表达状态转移，同时构建 193 项任务的 ABSBench。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究目标是社会模拟的真实性与可扩展性，既不涉及视觉或多模态推理，也未产生或使用 latent 推理状态；「原子操作组合」虽涉及状态转移，但与 LVR 的表示、证据筛选和停止决策无具体可核查的联系。
